record_scope_reconstruction: February6 and7 2024 road protests are split by day and crossing. Vidin ring-road obstruction allowed some cars to detour through the city, and February7 bridge authority distinguishes truck closure both ways from inbound-car restriction. Railway and ferry operations are outside the supported scope.

source_checks.finding: RRA February6 full report identifies machinery at Ruse customs roundabout and road toward Byala, with about two hours both ways. Vidin end18:00 was prospective.
BTA February6 original republication locates tractors on Vidin ring road, both carriageways to/from Bridge2; cargo stopped while cars could detour through the city.
Focus February7 reporter and bridge-company director identify10:00 restart, trucks both directions, cars inbound from Romania stopped, outbound cars via city allowed; previous day exceeded7hours.
BTA February8 follow-up confirms cargo stoppages exceeded7hours on each of preceding two days. Does not show continuous overnight closure.

Euronews Romania February7 full report confirms actual same-day interruption at all four routes, including Vama Veche and Negru Vodă. General almost-three-hour framing is not substituted for specific Vidin duration evidence.

Original OSM named Danube/Friendship Bridge structure links Ruse and Giurgiu; start_date1954. This combined road/rail structure locates only the affected road route. It is not the inland customs roundabout protest position, and no railway stoppage is inferred.

Original OSM named New Europe/Vidin-Calafat bridge structure matches Danube Bridge2 identity. This road/rail structure is a road-route reference only; E79 and Vidin ring-road blockade positions are not surveyed. The old Vidin ferry customs canopy3km west is explicitly rejected.

Original OSM customs canopy explicitly named ГКПП Кардам (БГ), version2 March2022. Named road checkpoint northeast of Kardam village, distinct from Kardam railway station and railway post buildings. Romanian police independently pairs Kardam with Negru Vodă.

Original OSM highway facility polygon explicitly names both Durankulak and Vama Veche, version1 July2022. Independently matches the Romanian police bilateral road-post pair. This is the checkpoint complex, not Durankulak village or the precise diverted-truck protest position.

Primary Romanian police notice explicitly pairs Giurgiu–Ruse, Calafat–Vidin, Vama Veche–Durankulak and Negru Vodă–Kardam; confirms road mode, not rail/ferry interchangeability. Used for geographic identity across episodes, not to establish March dates.
